newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Treasury has 9.7 bln real op deficit in '96.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Treasury has 9.7 bln real op deficit in '96.

text.p: Brazil's Treasury posted an operational deficit of 2.078 billion reais in December, bringing its operational deficit for 1996 to 9.778 bln reais, or 1.27 percent of GDP, it said in a statement.
The Treasury said its operational deficit in 1995 was 1.4 percent of GDP.
In primary terms, the Treasury's December result was a 1.105 billion real deficit. But the Treasury's primary result still closed the year with a 2.947 billion real surplus.

The Treasury said in an additional statement that it had decided to highlight the primary and operational results because these were used more often by international institutions. Previously, the Treasury had reported its results according to the cash concept.
In a table, it listed its cash concept results for 1996 as a deficit of 9.057 billion reais, after a deficit of 1.494 billion reais in December.

Total expenditure in the 12-month period was 91.698 billion reais against 89.973 billion reais in 1995. Total receipts stood at 94.644 billion reais last year compared with 93.839 billion reais the previous year.
The Treasury said its total interest payments for the year stood at 12.725 billion reais, versus 14.05 billion reais in 1995.
Payroll and social security costs were 41.711 billion reais in 1996 compared with 42.63 billion reais in 1995.
The more closely watched Central Bank figures, which include total public sector operational and primary budget data, were due out sometime over the next two weeks.
